notes:
Passed on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: this is a direct Driver with native.py rather than a PythonObjectDriver, because the upstream writeAnalog(Nsamples, Nchannels, values, autostart) takes an ndarray and the family table cannot express that call; no command wire syntax is involved. The driver covers the actuator's analog output voltage (one writable parameter, read back as the last value in the upstream write_buffer), the first device name, the AO and AI maximum rates, analog trigger support, the triggering-source count and the task write index. NOT COVERED: digital output (writeDigital), analog input acquisition (readAnalog/readDigital), counters, waveform generation, multi-channel tasks, and the upstream move_Abs/move_Rel/move_Home actions. The only write is bound to cap.device.configure.v1; no extension id was used. The output window is Limit.operator_required because the clone reads the card's range at run time and only falls back to a constant when the query fails; the values in site-limits.example.json are an example overlay only, not a claim about a card. The analog_output read is the last value written to the buffer, not a measured output voltage (docs/source/user_guide/scanner_details.rst:28). The hardware backend in native.py was not run and no hardware was attached; this package is model-authored and unreviewed, at R1 the loader does not refuse an unreviewed model-written hardware backend, so no review or hardware-run protection is claimed.
